correctness.rationale: The proof exhausts terminal sets by the number of occupied parts. If at least two parts are occupied, the induced graph is connected, so minimum Steiner trees use exactly the terminals. If one part is occupied by at least two terminals, exactly one outside vertex is necessary and sufficient, so the Steiner interval is the terminals together with all vertices outside that part. The singleton-terminal boundary and the all-singleton complete-graph case are handled separately. Exhaustive literal reconstruction through order 9 agrees on every subset and on both extremal parameters.

value.rationale: The result gives a natural complete classification for a standard graph-convexity invariant on the full complete-multipartite family, rather than another isolated minimum value. It shows extreme rigidity—there are exactly one plus the number of non-singleton parts Steiner sets—and simultaneously determines the entire size distribution and both lower and upper Steiner numbers. This is structurally informative for a family containing complete graphs, stars, bicliques, and Turán graphs, while remaining self-contained and exactly reproducible.
